about: One heat-relevant finding presented at COP31 (an addition after check-in 3, 19 November 2026): a survey commissioned by Wellcome of 1,000 clinicians in maternity and newborn care across Australia, Brazil, India, the UK and Zimbabwe. The five-country figures rest on Wellcome's own results page; the India-only figures, the COP31 presentation and a UN official's remark on health's share of climate finance rest on Down To Earth's report of the media briefing (16 November 2026) and are marked secondary. All figures are clinicians' reports of what they believe they have seen, not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Extreme heat is putting pregnant women and their babies at risk
Keeping Mothers Safe from Extreme Heat: A Global Call to Action

claims.where: Signal: clinicians' survey on heat in pregnancy
claims.text: In September 2026, Censuswide surveyed 1,000 practising healthcare professionals, 250 of them midwives, in pregnancy, childbirth, postnatal and newborn care across Australia, Brazil, India, the UK and Zimbabwe, for a survey commissioned by Wellcome.

claims.where: Signal: clinicians' survey on heat in pregnancy
claims.text: Across the five countries, 98% said they had cared for a pregnant woman, and 99% for a baby, whose health they believed extreme heat had harmed; 73% reported more heat-related complications in pregnant women and 76% in foetal or newborn health; 92% want more training and resources.

claims.where: Signal: clinicians' survey on heat in pregnancy (secondary)
claims.text: Among the 200 respondents in India, 62% reported more heat-related complications in pregnant women over five years and 66% in foetal or newborn health; 26% had seen pregnancy complications needing extra monitoring or treatment.

claims.where: Signal: clinicians' survey on heat in pregnancy (secondary)
claims.text: The findings were presented on 13 November on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya.

claims.where: Signal: clinicians' survey on heat in pregnancy (secondary)
claims.text: At the presentation, a UN Climate Change official said that about 1% of formal climate finance goes to health.
